task: Render ReviewResult.filteredFiles on the four formatters, and extend policy.agentsSkipped to the ones missing it, so a partial agentPolicy exclusion is never silent. Found by the PMB peer, verified in source and proved through the built formatters.
approved_by: user ("open the new PR for filteredFiles", 2026-08-31)
defect: --profile security runs security + adversarial, both carrying exclude ['**/*.md']. policyFilter.ts:47 only populates agentsSkipped when matchesAll(changedFiles, exclude) -- EVERY file must match. On a mixed diff the exclusion still strips the .md sections from those two agents' diffs and records them in filteredFiles, but agentsSkipped stays EMPTY, so the Policy line never renders. grep -rln filteredFiles src/ returns schema.ts, runner.ts, chunkRunner.ts -- all producers, no renderer anywhere. Proved through the built formatters on the peer's measured case (6 .md + 1 .sh): markdown said '**0 findings** | 4200ms', MCP said '✅ No findings', github-annotations returned an empty string, SARIF carried neither policy nor filteredFiles. Two agents reviewed 1 file of 7 and every surface reported clean.
correction_the_data_is_not_unreachable: The peer corrected an overstatement of mine and it is load-bearing for how this is described. `--format json` DOES carry filteredFiles: formatJson is `JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)` (formatter.ts:337-339), a raw dump, and runner.ts:932 spreads the field onto the result when non-empty -- so it appears with no formatter opting in. Verified in source and confirmed empirically. The accurate shape is therefore: all six RENDERED surfaces are dark, and the raw envelope carries it. That still justifies this change, but it means a consumer has a real interim mitigation today -- pass --format json and read filteredFiles -- rather than having to wait for a release. Do not describe the data as unreachable.
why_it_matters_more_than_earlyExit: earlyExit requires --fail-fast. This requires nothing: any diff mixing one non-markdown file with documentation silently narrows the security profile. A governed repo whose changes are mostly prose -- this one -- hits it on ordinary work. The presence of a single non-markdown file is what SUPPRESSES the signal, which is the opposite of the intuition a reader would apply.
design_decision: A partial exclusion is stated at the same tier as the existing Policy line -- a note in the body -- and does NOT flip the INCOMPLETE headline. Rationale: the exclusion is deliberate configuration, not a failure, and this repo's diffs are mostly mixed, so gating the headline on it would fire on nearly every run and train the reader to ignore the banner. That is the same line mcp/formatter.ts already draws for toolNotes, whose comment says a documented degraded mode does not earn the headline. The full-skip case renders a Policy note today, so parity says the partial case renders one too.
scope_boundary: FOUR formatters only. review.yml and vscode-extension are the fifth and sixth surfaces and are deliberately OUT of scope here: both need infrastructure that arrives with PR #83 (scripts/reviewIncompleteness.cjs, and the extension's copy of the envelope gaining incompleteness fields). Duplicating that module across two open PRs would create exactly the divergent-copy drift this work exists to remove. They follow once #83 merges, as a small addition to the shared module rather than a second copy of it.
verification: Mutation-prove every new test by reverting the behaviour and confirming the expected failure message, and count how many actually fail -- guards counted separately, never as regression evidence. Replay the peer's exact 6-.md-plus-1-.sh case through the built formatters and confirm each surface now names it.
